voce: Chapter six. Nine thirty a.m.: The market opens.
At the opening bell on August first, twenty twelve, the eighth server woke up.
sotto: At 9:30 a.m. ET, the eighth server begins executing.

voce: It began running the old Power Peg logic, code that was never meant to return.
Power Peg kept sending orders, because its code to count completed trades no longer worked.
oggetto: a glossy red faceless mannequin pressing an endless stream of buttons on a broken counter machine

voce: Nothing told it the job was done, so it simply kept going.
The SEC found Knight's system sent over four million executions in one hundred fifty-four stocks.
All of that, in roughly forty-five minutes.
oggetto: a giant glossy stopwatch with a cracked glass face, ticking above a trading floor

voce: The SEC found that over three hundred ninety-seven million shares traded as a result.
Reports noted abnormal price moves in many of the affected stocks.
sotto: Many affected stocks moved unusually at the open

voce: Traders across the street watched their screens, searching for an explanation.
Inside Knight, the clock was running, and nobody yet knew why.
